messages:
Mike H: Quick sync — ran a symmetric loadbench comparing kernel-v1 (baseline) vs kernel-v2 (new kv-prefetch + fuse) with continuous batching enabled. Setup: 64 tenants, 100 qps steady, ~2k token seqs, 8 GPU nodes. Observed a 9-13% p95 latency regression on kernel-v2 when batch_cap=64 + max_delay=12ms.

Perf Bot: bench summary: baseline p95=72ms, kernel-v2 p95=81ms, mean latency ~+6ms, tail CPU up ~18%, aggregate throughput ~equal. Replay job: gs://redwood-perf/runs/2026-03-01/symmetric-176999.

Anya R: Oof — do we know if kv-prefetch caused extra scheduling jitter?

Mike H: Prefetch was enabled for v2. I also saw an uptick in batch-size variance during microbursts which aligns with tail push.

Jia W: Can you paste the exact harness config and command?

Mike H: Command we ran: ```
./replay_harness --trace normalized_sym.trace --tenants 64 --qps 100 --seq-dist long_tail.json \
  --batch-cap 64 --max-delay-ms 12 --kernel kernel-v2 --kv-prefetch on --quant q4_0
```

Liam S: Attached is a quick histogram I grabbed from the run: larger mode at batch=48 but long right tail hitting 64 occasionally. That extra packing seems to push out some requests past the delay SLO.

Perf Bot: heatmap & per-tenant skew: gs://redwood-perf/plots/176999/heatmap.svg

Anya R: Hypothesis: kernel-v2's fused path has higher per-batch variance for short sequences (lower amortized setup cost on long seqs), and our selector currently picks kernel based on FLOPs estimate only. For short seqs it's picking v2 but the runtime cost model is off.

Jia W: Can we run a forced-selector variant (force kernel-v1 for seq<=256) to see delta?

Mike H: Did that quick test: forcing v1 for seq<=256 drops p95 to 74ms (almost baseline). Throughput unchanged. So it's pretty clear the selector mismatch is the primary driver.

Liam S: That implies we need a size-aware cost model (seq-length buckets) rather than a single scalar FLOPs heuristic. Also consider adding a small hysteresis to avoid oscillation when batch composition changes rapidly.

Anya R: Also: kv-prefetch could be contending with scheduler threads if it fires on many small requests; add a throttle that prefers prefetch only when batch_size >= 16?

Mike H: Agreed. Action items: 1) Jia to draft selector change: bucketed seq-length cost model + hysteresis. 2) Liam to prototype kv-prefetch throttle when batch < 16. 3) Perf: add continuous-batching probe to CI that runs a 1hr normalized symmetric replay.

Perf Bot: scheduled replay job: id=run-176999-smoke, ETA results in ~1h.

deploy-bot: FYI kernel-v2 rolling to canary queue=4. Pause recommended until selector fix.

Mike H: Please hold the canary rollout until we validate selector tweak. I'll open issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-1234 with logs and config.

Anya R: For the benchmark methodology notes — we should record: quantization identical, same scheduling config, same batch caps, and zero-init cache state. Also include a replay with KV cache warm vs cold to separate prefetch effects.

Jia W: I'll put a reproducibility checklist in the issue and schedule the 6-hour endurance replay overnight to catch fairness across tenants (tenant skew and drift).

Mike H: Thanks — let's reconvene after the overnight run. :thumbsup:
